Hunter S. Thompson (July 18, 1937 – February 20, 2005) was an American journalist and author, and the founder of the gonzo journalism movement, an experimental style of journalism where reporters involve themselves in the action to such a degree that they become central figures of their stories.

The Rum Diary was one of his earliest novels that was written in the early 1960s but was not published until 1998. The manuscript was discovered among Thompson's papers by friend and actor Johnny Depp. Mimicking Thompson's own life at the time, the story involves a journalist who, in the 1950s, moves from New York to work for a major newspaper in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
